images.title: Cancel plus three with minus three
images.purpose: Show that +3 followed by −3 brings the lift back to the ground floor, so the total is 0.
images.composition: Two equal arrows side by side in the middle, both between the same two level lines, with the equation centred below.
images.exact_structure: Two horizontal grey #6B7280 level lines: the lower marked 0 as the ground floor and the upper marked +3, with a clear gap between them. A teal #0072B2 arrow of exact length from the lower line to the upper line on the left, and an amber #E69F00 arrow of exactly the same length from the upper line back to the lower line on the right. A reddish purple #CC79A7 dot on the lower line. Below, centred, the equation line. Exactly 2 level lines, 2 equal arrows, 1 dot, 1 equation.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any extra floor, dot, arrow or row beyond the counts stated
unequal floor rows or unequal arrow lengths
images.takeaway: Pressing the opposite number cancels the move and returns to 0.
images.description: Two level lines, 0 below and +3 above; a teal arrow up and an equal amber arrow back down to 0, with (+3) + (−3) = 0 below.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say how far up the teal arrow goes and what the amber arrow must do to return.

image_decisions.why: Cancelling a move is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
